calls.reasoning: Amazon guided Q3 2026 net sales to $197-202B, assuming about 80bp of FX headwind, and analyst consensus is about $202.2B. Over the last 8 quarters, actual revenue landed between -$0.7B and +$3.7B against the top of guidance (median about +$0.5-1B). The only shortfall, Q4'24, came in a quarter when the dollar strengthened. The dollar did firm in late September after the Fed hike, but it was weaker in August and early September, so FX for the whole quarter is about neutral to a slight headwind. AWS strength (37% growth in Q2, capacity sold out) supports a modest beat. The Prime Day shift into Q2 is already in the guidance. Median is about $203.0B. No human prediction market was found.
calls.reconciliation: Main factual dispute: FX during Q3 relative to the late-July guidance assumption. Run 1 called it flat. Runs 2 and 3 cited a DXY rise of about 2% after the Sep 16 hike. Run 1's own figures (DXY 100.35 end-July, 99.55 end-August, 98.61 on Sep 9, 100.98 on Sep 25) show the dollar weaker for most of the quarter and stronger only at the end. That points to a near-neutral to slight average headwind, not the ~$0.5B Run 3 assumed. I had no web access, so I could not check the Q1'26 guidance top (178.5 vs. unknown). That leaves the size of the beat history somewhat uncertain, and I let it widen the spread. On judgment: Amazon has a steady habit of landing just above its guidance top, which with the top at $202B puts the median near $203B. Run 2's more aggressive median relies on beating consensus by 1-2%, which is less well supported once the FX drag is counted. I kept the beat-vs-guidance-top reference class that all runs used.
